judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single flat prohibition; its wording is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.2(ii) lists "retirement, resignation, expulsion" of a Member as a dissolution event, which presupposes a resignation that this section forbids — the two cannot both operate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long procedural code; the friction is between "A Majority present in person or by proxy" as a quorum (a vote count used as a head count) and the separate "Majority Vote" decision rule in (viii).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (xi) lets a Majority act by written consent for any matter "unless otherwise provided," which sits against unanimity requirements in Sections 13.1, 14.3, 15.2(i) and 17.10; with a 51/49 split DMSA alone constitutes a quorum and a Majority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It designates Directors as Managers "for purposes of the Act" — a term the Agreement never defines (the defined term is "Maine Act").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Board management is made "Subject to Section 5.1," while Section 5.1 defers to powers vested in the Board, producing a circular allocation of control between a one-director member and a two-director member.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed notice mechanics; "by any other means of communication" is a loose catch-all after a specific list but the point is procedural.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.3's quorum rule and Section 7.4's notice duty of the Secretary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It excepts matters "otherwise provided in Section 6.9," but there is no Section 6.9 in this Agreement — a live cross-reference error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The tie-break sends deadlocked Board matters to the Members, where a Majority (DMSA's 51 votes) decides, which would let DMSA carry matters that Section 6.8 requires the Board to approve unanimously.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain procedural authorisation for telephonic meetings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 5.5(x) for Member meetings without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It bars committees from taking "any of the actions described in Section 6.9," a section that does not exist, and otherwise gives committees "all the powers and authority of the Board."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the intended reference is plainly Section 6.8, a literal reading would let a one-Director committee take the very actions Section 6.8 reserves to unanimous Board approval.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Its own terms are clear, but it is numbered "Section 6.6" — the same number as the immediately following Removal of Directors section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(x) requires unanimous Board approval for contracts with Directors, which pulls against this section's simple grant of authority to "fix the compensation of Directors."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Substantively clear (each Member removes its own elected Director) but it carries a duplicate section number, and the numbering error shifts every later cross-reference in the Article.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Sections 6.1 and 5.5(ii)'s allocation of one Director to LSB and two to DMSA; the duplicate numbering is what explains the stray "Section 6.9" references in 6.3 and 6.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short agency statement, definite in scope ("to the extent of their powers set forth in this Agreement").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Section 7.6 for Officers and consistent with Section 5.1's denial of individual Member authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item (iii) — no distributions "other than to reimburse DMSA for initial capital contributions" — is a one-sided carve-out whose scope is undefined, and items (viii) and (xiv) turn on the unmeasured word "material."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That carve-out cannot be reconciled with Section 9.1 (distributions in proportion to Percentage Interests), Section 4.3(i) (returns of capital pro rata and only with all Members' consent) or Section 9.2 (Board sets amounts), and Sections 6.3 and 6.5 mis-cite this section as 6.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and conventional officer-appointment mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Removal "by the affirmative vote of a majority of the Board" coexists with Section 6.8(x)'s unanimity for termination of Officer employment contracts, a modest tension between office and contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "General and active management of the business" is broad, but the execution authority is carefully bounded by express exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives the President management of the business while Section 6.1 gives that to the Board and Section 5.1 reserves residual power to the Members — a three-way layering that Section 6.8 only partly resolves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard succession provision, expressly conditional ("if any").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-referenced by Section 7.2 and consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Duties are enumerated specifically plus "such other duties as may be prescribed"; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.1(iii) and 2.6 add Secretary duties (updating Schedule A, filings) not repeated here, an incompleteness rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional treasurer's duties, stated precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 10.1-10.2 and 6.8(xi) on deposit banks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, bounded agency statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Section 6.7 and consistent with Section 7.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Fiduciary duty of loyalty and care similar to those of directors and officers of business corporations" imports an entire corporate standard by the vague word "similar," and is prefaced by an undefined "Except to the extent provided herein."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7 expressly relieves DMSA of its fiduciary duties as a Director and Section 12.3 replaces duties existing at law, so the duty this section imposes is contradicted elsewhere in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean pro rata allocation rule keyed to a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.3 distributes liquidation proceeds by Capital Account balances rather than Percentage Interests, a difference that only bites on winding up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) refers to how Members "shared Interest Profits and Losses," a garbled phrase, and clause (iv) says the provisions "are intended to comply" twice over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended compliance with § 704(b) sits uneasily with the Profits/Losses definition, which is pure § 703(a) taxable income with no capital-account book adjustments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard § 704(c) provision stated in statutory terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.4 and 8.2(iv).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: Net Cash Flow distributions go pro rata to Percentage Interests.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(iii) permits distributions only to reimburse DMSA's initial capital contributions absent unanimous Board approval, and Section 4.3(ii)(a) directs payment of DMSA's invoices ahead of Members generally — both cut across the pro rata rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence conferring unfettered Board timing discretion; clear, if one-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives the Board the call while the Net Cash Flow definition gives the reserve decision to "the Members," and Section 6.8(iii) overrides it with a unanimity requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow legal-compliance limitation, precisely stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the corresponding sentence in Section 4.3(i) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed withholding mechanics; the internal reference "pursuant to this 9.4" drops the word Section but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Articles VIII and XI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires books kept with "a copy of this Agreement and of the Certificate" — "Certificate" is never defined — and conditions inspection on "reasonable times" and "any purpose reasonably related" to a Member's interest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined instrument is "Articles" under Article I, so the reference is to a document this Agreement does not create; the inspection right is otherwise unqualified elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mandate to keep books on the accrual method "for both financial and tax reporting purposes" is clear on its own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Net Cash Flow definition requires determination "in accordance with the cash receipts and disbursements method of accounting," a direct methodological contradiction with this section that bears on every distribution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise statutory designation with a definite ten-day notice duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 11.2's partnership treatment and Article X's tax-return obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single declarative sentence with no room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 11.1 and the Article VIII allocation regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard LLC limited-liability language, carefully qualified by "solely by reason of being a Member or Manager."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.4, 15.5 and 4.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is visibly broken: subsection (i) ends at "gross negligence or willful misconduct" and the section then resumes mid-sentence about reliance on persons of "professional or expert competence," with the operative reliance clause missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exculpation it gives sits against Section 7.7's imposition of corporate-style fiduciary duties on Directors and Officers, and against Section 12.7's separate release of DMSA.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Good faith reliance on the provisions of this Agreement" as an immunity, plus a wholesale replacement of duties "to the extent" the Agreement restricts them, leaves the residual duty boundary unfixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.7 affirmatively imposes fiduciary duties of loyalty and care while this section replaces duties existing at law or equity — the two point in opposite directions on the same question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully bounded indemnity with an express gross-negligence/willful-misconduct carve-out and an asset-only limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17.11 says nothing confers rights on any Person "except the Members and Managers," yet this section confers indemnity on all Covered Persons including employees and Affiliates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional advancement clause tied to an undertaking to repay; clear mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Section 12.4, which is intact; the only friction is again with Section 17.11's limitation of beneficiaries.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is cut off after "against any liability that may be asserted," so the scope of the permitted insurance is simply missing from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is permissive only and does not contradict Sections 12.4 or 3.2(i)(h).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is broken ("and the Company the income or profits derived therefrom" is missing a verb), and the restraint on LSB turns on "such services" with no clear antecedent and on "the business," an undefined and unbounded phrase with no time or geographic limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relieves DMSA of "its fiduciary duties as a Director" although DMSA is a Member and not a Director under Section 6.1, and it contradicts Section 7.7's imposition of loyalty and care duties while its scope depends on the Section 3.1 purpose clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires consent "of the LLC," a term never defined, and its "Proprietary Information" definition is a closed list of business categories with no confidentiality period, no carve-out for public information and no definition of what "kept confidential" requires of "all efforts and actions."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It binds LSB and DMSA symmetrically while Section 12.7 expressly authorises DMSA to compete and to take opportunities for its own account, which is hard to square with a duty to keep all Company efforts confidential.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear two-condition admission mechanic requiring unanimous Member approval.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.8 lets the Board waive "any transfer restrictions contained in this Agreement," which could be read to bypass this unanimity for transferee-members under Section 16.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Their respective Interest of the Company's income" is a garbled use of the defined term, though the tax mechanics are otherwise conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VIII allocations and Section 13.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Without complying with the terms of this Agreement" is circular — it forbids assignment except in compliance with unspecified terms found nowhere in the Article it heads.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The actual transfer restrictions sit in Article XVI, while Section 14.2 voids assignments "in violation of this Article XIV," so the prohibition and the sanction point at different Articles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in effect (invalidity plus no liability for refusing distributions), but it is keyed to violations "of this Article XIV," which contains almost no substantive restrictions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The operative restrictions are in Article XVI (Sections 16.2, 16.3, 16.5, 16.6), so a transfer breaching Article XVI arguably escapes this voiding provision altogether.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clear prohibition subject to unanimous written consent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.2 defines "transfer" to include a transfer "as security" and Section 16.8 lets the Board alone waive any transfer restriction — which would override the all-Member consent this section requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short negative rule with a clear trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13.1 and 15.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of member-level events (death, retirement, resignation, expulsion, bankruptcy) is followed by a catch-all keyed to the Maine Act, and "expulsion" appears nowhere else in the Agreement as a procedure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.4 forbids a Member from resigning before winding up, so subsection (ii)'s resignation trigger is a dissolution event that the Agreement elsewhere makes impossible; with only two Members the "remaining Members" cure clause reduces to one person.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Members shall continue to distribute Interest Profits and Losses" is garbled and misattributes distribution to the Members when the Board is winding up, and "a reasonable time" is left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It distributes liquidation proceeds by Capital Account balances, whereas Sections 8.1 and 9.1 allocate and distribute by Percentage Interests — the two measures diverge because Capital Accounts reflect the unequal contributions on Schedule A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise two-condition termination rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.3 and 15.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear "look solely to the Company's assets" language with an express no-recourse conclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.1, 4.3(iii) and 4.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Each transfer ... shall be made on Schedule A" is an odd mechanic (a schedule as a transfer register) but its meaning is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) makes the Secretary responsible for updating Schedule A and says such changes are not amendments, so record ownership can shift without Member action.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It promises restrictions "set forth below" and defines transfer expansively, then imposes a forfeiture of voting and "dividend" rights — a corporate term with no LLC referent — while the failure "continues."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Article XIV assignment and pledge rules overlap this definition of transfer, and Section 16.4's waiver machinery cross-refers to Sections 16.9-16.11 that do not exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear two-branch validity condition for transferees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.1 requires unanimous Member approval before a Person becomes a Member, which this section does not mention — a gap between becoming a party and being admitted.
